title: The monastic day
hookLine: up in the night to sing psalms, then work, study, silence

cards: Somewhere past midnight, a house goes very still. The fridge hums, the floor creaks, and a mind left alone can circle for hours. At that same hour in a Kentucky monastery, a bell rings in the dark.
The monks get up, pull on their robes, and walk quietly into a cold church. Nobody's scrolling. They open their books and sing psalms to God while the whole county sleeps.

teach.b: First, the night. The first prayer of a Trappist day is called Vigils, from the Latin for keeping watch. The bell rings in the small hours, long before dawn.
They sing psalms and listen to long readings from scripture and the saints, in the dark, before a single email exists. Second, the rhythm.
The Rule of Saint Benedict builds the day around set hours of prayer, taking its cue from two lines in the Psalms.
In the Douay-Rheims: "Seven times a day I have given praise to thee." And: "I rose at midnight to give praise to thee."

So the day goes Vigils, then Lauds at dawn, short hours through the morning and afternoon, Vespers at evening, and Compline before bed. Benedict's Rule asks that all one hundred fifty psalms be sung over each week.
Third, everything in between. Work: in Merton's day, fields, barns, and later the cheese and fruitcake Gethsemani still sells. Study: slow, prayerful reading of scripture, called lectio divina.
And silence, most of all the great silence after Compline, until morning. Fourth, why the dark.
Some monks compare the night office to a watchman on the city wall, awake for everyone who's asleep.

teach.h: I ROSE AT MIDNIGHT TO GIVE PRAISE.
teach.b: Merton wrote about those dark hours in his journals. For the monks, the first word of the day isn't a notification. It's a psalm.

how: Monks and nuns pray the Liturgy of the Hours in choir through the day and night, and many lay Catholics pray shorter forms of it, especially Morning and Evening Prayer.

o: the last prayer of the day, before bed
the monks' night prayer, before dawn

the Rule spreads the whole psalter across the week.

games.q: it's the middle of the night at Gethsemani and the bell rings. you're a monk, and you're tired. what happens next?
o: get up and go sing psalms in the dark church
games.why: the whole community rises for Vigils. some monks describe it as keeping watch for the world while it sleeps.

practice: Sit as if it were very early and the house still asleep; let your shoulders drop and breathe slowly. Think of one person who's asleep, or can't sleep, tonight, and keep watch for them for a minute, like the watchman on the wall.
If you pray, you can pray one line of a psalm you know.

wordCard.voice: Vigils. The night prayer of monks and nuns, from the Latin for keeping watch. The first prayer of the monastic day, sung before dawn. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the watches of the night, the name of the monks' night prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: pray before the world wakes. For the monks, the dark is for keeping watch. That's day two hundred seventy-six.
